name: Narrow 4-2-2-2

slots.why: Support full-back is the only wide player on the left, so he provides the width.
Central defender. Cover is the alternate, as is a Ball-Playing Defender (Defend), who can find the double pivot or the half-space attacking midfielders with shorter passing.
Central defender on the right. Cover is the alternate, but only one Cover can be used.
Support full-back on the right, the only width on that side.
Ball-winning midfielder wins the ball back and starts the press.
Deep-lying playmaker distributes from the base of the midfield.
Shadow striker presses from the half-space and runs beyond the strikers into the box.
Attacking midfielder (Support) links the pivot with the strikers and creates from the other half-space.
Deep-lying forward holds up the ball and links with the attacking midfielders. Complete Forward is the alternate.
Advanced Forward runs in behind the defence. Poacher is the alternate.

description: A narrow 4-2-2-2 with a double pivot, two attacking midfielders in the half-spaces and two strikers, giving six players in the middle of the pitch.
whyGood: Six central players make a compact, well-connected team that overloads the middle and presses as a unit.
whyThisShape: The two attacking midfielders sit in the half-spaces between the opposition's centre-backs and full-backs, and with the double pivot and two strikers, six players occupy the middle of the pitch. Passes between them are short, and the team presses as a compact unit. The only width comes from the full-backs, so the shape depends on them.
whenToUse: When your best players are central and you lack wingers, especially against a team with two central midfielders who will be overrun.
whenNotToUse: Against sides that attack down the flanks and outnumber your full-backs, and when your full-backs cannot cover a whole flank.

instructionRationale.Fairly Narrow: Keep the central combinations close; the selected wide defenders supply the outside outlets.
instructionRationale.Shorter Passing: Use the short connections supplied by the selected midfield and supporting forwards.
instructionRationale.Higher Tempo: Move the ball before the opponent resets, using the receivers and runners supplied by the roles.
instructionRationale.Counter-Press: Challenge immediately after losing possession, with the roles around the ball supporting the first pressure.
instructionRationale.Higher Line of Engagement: Engage the build-up earlier, accepting that the forwards need support from the midfield behind them.
instructionRationale.Standard Defensive Line: Keep the back line at its mentality-relative default rather than explicitly pushing it up or dropping it.
instructionRationale.Counter: Use the forward runners immediately after a regain, before the opponent can recover its shape.
instructionRationale.Distribute To Full Backs: The selected outlets match where this tactic starts its build-up or releases pressure.
instructionRationale.Low Crosses: A starting delivery choice for the receiving roles, to review against the actual forwards.
instructionRationale.More Urgent Pressing: Challenge more often inside the selected engagement zone without making the settled press maximal.
instructionRationale.Never Time Wasting: The kick-off baseline; review deliberately when score and time justify a different policy.
instructionRationale.Roll It Out: Start possession through the chosen short outlets instead of routinely contesting a long kick.

keyRequirements: Full-backs who provide all the width
A ball-winner and a playmaker in the pivot
A shadow striker and a creative attacking midfielder
setupNotes: All three phases have been reviewed. Standard sliders are relative to the chosen mentality; unselected toggles intentionally leave FM to choose the response.
Player instructions use the selected role and duty defaults unless additional instructions are listed. Crossing and overlap settings are starting choices to review against the selected players.
